summary: pid_separation_power.py used rounded built-in species masses instead of CODATA 2022 / PDG 2026 values; cherenkov_angle.py uses the same table.

database_specific.introduced_basis: the defective code is in the script as first released (hep-research 0.3.0, commit 351029c0)

observables: PID separation, time of flight and dE/dx of the named species (pid_separation_power.py)
Cherenkov photon yield, threshold momentum and angle of named species (cherenkov_angle.py)
impact.bias: relative shifts of order 1e-9: for He4 at p = 40 GeV/c, n = 1.05 the expected photons 68.07557496982115 -> 68.07557492992738, threshold 11.642377257681904 -> 11.642377294538912 GeV (6e-10 and 3e-9 relative); masses e, p, d, He3, He4 and the Bethe-Bloch electron mass changed in the last digits
impact.trigger: a species given by name (e, p, d, He3, He4) rather than by an explicit mass

outputs.how_to_recognize: JSON on stdout: pid_separation_power.py with mode, species_a and species_b (mass_gev), observable, n_sigma; cherenkov_angle.py with expected_photons and photon_regime (it used the same mass table)

remedy: no action is needed for design estimates; rerun with a release that has the fix where a result quotes more than 8 significant digits
